AT1, AT2, AT3, AT6 red; AT4 red because BOTH --replace mutations apply ('replaced 1 occurrence' in tools/linux_trial_sandbox.sh and in tools/isolated_trial_adapter.py), the mutated suite exits 1 with 'AssertionError: 40 != 0', and no result line carries UNSUPPORTED; AT5, AT7 (16/16), AT8 (79/79) green; S01 and S07 green guards; S02-S06, S08-S16 red as declared; new S17 red (flag unknown, exit 2, no FAIL lines, no probe) and S18 red (no FULL line, sandbox calls without a probe). Positive control (10-positive-control-A.txt): my rev-1 implementation (helpers/rev2/implement.py unchanged; the pinned texts are identical in rev 2) in a detached worktree whose .git is a FILE, on <B> (approved-contract commit) on <A>: ALL 26 commands (AT1-AT8, S01-S18) exit 0 on this restricted host, both before and after the single attempt commit, including S17 and S18 and the hardened S14. Simulated capable host (PATH shim, helpers/rev2/capable_shim.sh): AT1 and AT2 capable branches exit 0, and the amended AT4 capable branch holds ('FAIL: test_linux_sandbox_blocks_cross_trial_files_and_network', 'AssertionError: 40 != 0', EXPECTATIONS HELD). That is gating-logic simulation only. This host (kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1) cannot exercise any capable-host branch; the real proof stays with feature 104 AT5-AT8 and nothing in 103 may be credited with it.

Negative controls (12-negative-controls-A.txt): 53 mutants (rev-1's 38 plus N1, N2, N3, N5, N6 from the amendment and m23-m29, m31-m33), each a fresh worktree with ONE defect, 24 checks run restricted plus AT1/AT2/AT4 again under the simulated-capable shim. 51 of 53 are caught by their targeted check. Rev-1 survivors now die: m05c (flag masks sandbox-test failures once the probe passed) -> S17; m18 (every skip counted as UNSUPPORTED) -> S18; m08b (second subprocess call in a new class) and m08c (aliased import) -> S14; new m23 (import-as alias in a class), m24 (__import__), m25 (two calls in the probe), m26 (os.popen), m27 (Popen in the probe), m28 (the word subprocess outside the probe) -> S14; m29 (flag turns all-five-failures into exit 0) -> S17; m32 (substring match on 'UNSUPPORTED') -> S18. Amended AT4 and N1-N6: N1 probe always unavailable -> restricted AT4 rc 0 (correct there), capable AT4c rc 1, also S10/S11/S17/S18; N2 probe goes through linux_trial_sandbox.sh -> restricted AT4 rc 1, plus S09-S13/S17/S18; N3 decorator silently returns when available -> capable AT4c rc 1, S10, S17, S18; N4 exec line already removed in tree (m22) and N5 Landlock call already removed in tree -> AT4 rc 3 (mutation precondition, fail-closed) on both branches; N6 cross-trial assertion weakened -> capable AT4c rc 1, S08. The amended AT4 therefore discriminates on the capable branch (simulated) and the restricted branch's power (N2) is intact. Every requested defect fails its targeted check: required mode exits 0 while UNSUPPORTED (AT1, AT4, S09, S11, S12); probe via shell or repo code (S14, S09-S13); unsandboxed fallback in script or wrapper (AT5/S07/S14/S15, AT1/AT2/AT4/S09); env read relaxing the mode (S14); flag masking (AT3, S13, S17); sandbox script, adapter or test body modified (AT5, S07, S14, S08); second subprocess call (S14); out-of-scope file (S02, S15); another feature's status flipped (S02, S15); extra phase-YAML key (S03); README or CHANGELOG pin altered (S04, S05, S06).

The two survivors are documented limits, not defects. m04b (environment read obfuscated as vars(os)['env'+'iron']) survives because a regex cannot see it; S14's own text now says so and assigns it to Mode B diff review (the validator carried that forward). m14 (decorator without functools.wraps) is behaviourally inert because unittest names results from the attribute, not __name__. m10b is a control, not a defect: a legitimate 103-only feature_list status flip keeps S02 green and is rejected only by the attempt-root check S15, as designed.

S17 and S18 are self-contained and replayable from the repo root (11-s17-s18-self-contained.txt): both build their PATH shim, the unshare log and (S18) the jsonschema ImportError stub inside tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(), read only .agent/contracts/103.json and tools/test_convergent_review.py by repo-relative path, and contain no scratchpad, /home, /tmp or /usr path, no chdir, no network. They passed twice each from the root of a FRESH clone at the attempt commit in a different directory under env -i. S18 genuinely needs Landlock in the kernel (it runs the five tests for real through the unchanged adapter, no namespaces); that works on this host and the contract says so (hazard 10) and says to escalate, never weaken, if it fails elsewhere. The Evaluator's re-run of S18 is therefore a Landlock-dependent check; it is not run in CI.

Testability (13-testability-A.txt): all 26 commands signal their exit through sys.exit/assert/test $? with no pipelines, no || true, no network, no wall clock beyond bounded timeouts, no absolute paths (static scan, 26/26 clean). Three consecutive passes of AT1-AT4, S09-S14, S17, S18 in the attempt worktree gave identical results and timings (S09 ~9 s, the others <7 s; AT7 ~11-25 s and AT8 ~26 s depending on load). Commands are repo-root-relative by declaration. scratch_run copies the worktree including the .git FILE and works. Never run AT7/AT8 concurrently or alongside the scratch_run checks; I ran everything strictly sequentially (the mutant sweep ran no AT7/AT8).

Residual notes, none blocking: (a) S14 still scans added comments and docstrings, so any added comment that merely contains the word subprocess outside the probe, or sudo/chmod/environ, false-fails (m28); hazard 9 now tells the Generator so. (b) AT4's restricted-host branch is inert by construction, as the contract's expected_outcome now states; it proves only the UNSUPPORTED outcome. (c) NDEBT-046 stands: no test detects removal of the namespaces alone; AT4 proves isolation removal is detected through the Landlock/filesystem leg, which is what 104 AT7/AT8 will exercise. (d) Required mode is enforced only through the module's own entry point; 'python3 -m unittest' reports the skips but exits 0 and prints no CONFORMANCE line (nothing in the repo invokes it that way). (e) 104 CI must install jsonschema (AT1/AT2 capable branches forbid the word skipped) and run on a Landlock-capable kernel.

Host safety: no sysctl, AppArmor, sudo or capability change; all experiments ran in scratch clones and worktrees under the scratchpad (removed afterwards); the contract file and every tracked file other than this verdict were not modified (the contract is byte-identical to the one reviewed); PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. New evidence: 08-14 and helpers/rev2/ under the S02-allowlisted prefix .agent/evidence/103-qa-adversarial-contract-review/ (S02 run verbatim in the shared tree lists no extra path, 14-schema-and-s02-allowlist.txt).

final_verdict.summary: APPROVED at contract revision 2 (103-contract attempt 3/3). All four rev-1 issues are closed and re-proved by execution: AT1-AT8 are byte-identical to <A>; base states are red for the intended reasons; a contract-faithful implementation turns all 26 commands (AT1-AT8, S01-S18) green on this restricted host from an attempt worktree; 51 of 53 injected defects are caught by their targeted check (the 2 survivors are documented, non-defect limits); S17 and S18 are self-contained and replayable from the repo root. No capable-host pass is claimed: the capable branches of AT1, AT2 and AT4 were only simulated and remain with feature 104 AT5-AT8.

history.summary: REJECTED at contract revision 1 (103-contract attempt 2/3 consumed; revision 2 is the last). The suite is otherwise sound and runnable: AT1-AT8 are verbatim, every base state is red for the intended reason (or green as a declared guard), a contract-faithful implementation turns all 24 commands green on this restricted host from an attempt worktree, and 32 of the 38 injected defects are caught. Blocking: (1, high) AT4's capable-host branch is unsatisfiable -- removing unshare leaves all 54 tests passing -- yet the contract, the feature description and 104 AT7/AT8 rely on it; (2, medium) --allow-unsupported-isolation masking sandbox-test failures on a partial-capability host passes every check; (3, medium) counting ordinary skips as UNSUPPORTED passes every check; (4, low) S14 misses a second subprocess call inside a class or via an aliased import.

issues.criterion: AT4 (verification[3], 1-based AT4) and the contract claims built on it: 'on a capable host AT4's sandbox-removal mutation must turn test_linux_sandbox_blocks_cross_trial_files_and_network into a FAIL line' (verification[3].expected_outcome; design_notes.available_isolation_branch; design_notes.capable_host_obligation.discharge; non_goals bullet 5). The same sentence is in the feature-103 description and is the pass condition of feature 104 AT7/AT8.
issues.evidence: Falsified by execution, not by reasoning. (a) At base on this host the mutated suite (exec unshare ... replaced by exec) prints 'Ran 54 tests ... OK' with test_linux_sandbox_blocks_cross_trial_files_and_network ... ok (02-base-states.txt AT4 block; contract entry for AT4 says only 'no result line carries UNSUPPORTED' and hides that the mutation is inert). (b) The mutated run never calls unshare, so its result is host-independent. Forced capable branch (PATH shim: probe exits 0, so AT4's own cap is True; evidence 05-coverage-gaps.txt F1): scratch_run reports 'Ran 54 tests / OK / CONFORMANCE: FULL', 'FAIL exit status is non-zero', 'FAIL output matches ^(FAIL|ERROR): test_linux_sandbox_blocks_cross_trial_files_and_network', EXPECTATION FAILED, rc 1. Cause: the test's network leg is `socket.connect(('127.0.0.1',9))` and passes on any OSError (ConnectionRefused included), and the file leg is enforced by the Landlock half (isolated_trial_adapter.py), so removing the namespaces is undetectable. (c) A mutation the test does detect exists: disabling the Landlock restriction in the adapter gives 'FAIL: test_linux_sandbox_blocks_cross_trial_files_and_network ... AssertionError: 40 != 0' (05 F1c). (d) AT4's restricted-host branch is also inert with respect to the mutation: it passes by UNSUPPORTED alone, whether or not the mutation is applied. Consequence: the capable-host obligation as written can never be discharged; 104 AT7/AT8 would fail on a real capable runner.
issues.required_fix: Contract revision 2 (final permitted) must stop asserting what execution refutes: remove or correct the mutation-turns-the-test-red claim in verification[3].expected_outcome, design_notes.available_isolation_branch, design_notes.capable_host_obligation.discharge and non_goals bullet 5; state that AT4's mutation is inert for the cross-trial test (host-independent: mutated suite exits 0 with CONFORMANCE: FULL once the probe passes) and that evidence of the available-isolation branch rests on S10 (+ the new flag/skip checks below) only. AT4's text is operator-fixed (acceptance_test must stay byte-identical, S01), so the Orchestrator must separately route an amendment request to the Planner/operator for AT4's capable branch, the 103 description's CAPABLE-HOST OBLIGATION sentence and 104 AT7/AT8 (candidate valid negative control: disable the Landlock restriction, 05 F1c; or a test whose network leg is discriminating). Do not claim AT4 capable-host coverage anywhere until then.

issues.criterion: 'The flag never masks any other failure' (feature description; mode_switch.flag_scope) on the available-isolation branch: S10 runs without the flag, AT3/S13 mask-check only non-sandbox failures or the unavailable branch.
issues.evidence: Mutant m05c (the wrapper converts an AssertionError from a sandbox-test body into an UNSUPPORTED skip when --allow-unsupported-isolation is given) passes all 24 verification commands (04-negative-controls.txt, corrected re-run line: AT1..S16 all =0). Directly: S10's shim (probe ok, sandbox refused 97) plus the flag gives positive control rc=1 with 5 FAIL lines and 'CONFORMANCE: NOT FULL (run unsuccessful)', mutant rc=0 with 'UNSUPPORTED' lines and exit 0 (05-coverage-gaps.txt F3). This is exactly the partial-capability host the contract calls the residual case, so a flag that hides real sandbox failures there would pass the gate unnoticed.
issues.required_fix: Add a supplementary check (a second S10 run or a new S17), host-independent: with S10's shim (probe exits 0 only for exactly `--user --map-root-user true`, anything else exits 97) and --allow-unsupported-isolation, require exactly the five `FAIL:` lines, no `UNSUPPORTED`, no `skipped`, non-zero exit, no allow note, the exact line `CONFORMANCE: NOT FULL (run unsuccessful)`. Add its evidence file to scope.files_create and to the S01 count.

issues.criterion: Outcome vocabulary: UNSUPPORTED is 'counted by prefix, so ordinary skips (the pre-existing jsonschema-ImportError skipTests) are never mistaken for it' (design_notes.outcome_vocabulary; non_goals bullet 6).
issues.evidence: Mutant m18 (count every skip as UNSUPPORTED instead of testing the prefix) passes all 24 verification commands (04-negative-controls.txt). Behavioural proof (05-coverage-gaps.txt F4): capable-host shim + a jsonschema stub that raises ImportError (only ordinary skips occur): positive control rc=0 'CONFORMANCE: FULL'; mutant rc=1 'CONFORMANCE: NOT FULL (UNSUPPORTED isolation-dependent tests: 5)'. Every existing S-check uses an isolation-less or failing shim, so the prefix test is never discriminated.
issues.required_fix: Add a supplementary check: capable shim (probe ok; sandbox call drops the 8 namespace flags and execs the adapter; helpers/capable_shim.sh in the evaluator evidence is a working model) plus a PYTHONPATH `jsonschema.py` that raises ImportError; require exit 0, the bare line `CONFORMANCE: FULL`, no `UNSUPPORTED`, and five ordinary `skipped` result lines. (It also exercises the capable branch of the gating logic for the first time.)

issues.criterion: 'The module gains exactly one subprocess call -- the fixed-argv probe (S14)' and 'no unsandboxed fallback by construction' (design_notes.no_unsandboxed_fallback item 3).
issues.evidence: S14's spawns() ignores calls inside any ClassDef and only matches the attribute form `subprocess.<run|Popen|call|check_call|check_output>`. Mutants m08b (second subprocess.run inside a new helper class) and m08c (`from subprocess import run as _run`, then `_run(...)`) pass all 24 commands (04-negative-controls.txt); the plain second call m08a is caught (S14=1). `os.popen/os.exec*/os.spawn*` are also outside the forbidden regex. S08 explicitly permits new helper classes.
issues.required_fix: Harden S14: in the added lines (git diff -U0 88959c9) every occurrence of `\bsubprocess\b|\bPopen\b|posix_spawn|os\.(popen|exec\w*|spawn\w*)` must lie on the one import line or inside probe_user_namespace_isolation (resolve by AST line ranges), regardless of class nesting or import aliasing; keep the existing exactly-one-new-module-level-call assertion.

missing_acceptance_coverage: Flag never masks a real failure of the five sandbox-dependent tests when isolation was reported available (partial-capability host) -- see issue S10; AT3 and S13 cover only non-sandbox failures and the unavailable branch.
Ordinary (jsonschema-ImportError) skips are never counted as UNSUPPORTED and leave a capable host at CONFORMANCE: FULL -- see issue S09-S13.
AT4 capable-host branch: no valid discharge exists (see issue AT4); not coverable by this feature's checks.
unsupported_claims: design_notes.available_isolation_branch: 'AT4's mutation, which on a capable host must turn test_linux_sandbox_blocks_cross_trial_files_and_network into a FAIL line' is refuted by execution (05-coverage-gaps.txt F1: Ran 54 tests / OK / CONFORMANCE: FULL).
design_notes.capable_host_obligation.discharge and non_goals bullet 5: 'AT4's capable branch = feature 104 AT7/AT8' cannot be discharged as written.
design_notes.no_unsandboxed_fallback item 3: 'exactly one subprocess call (S14)' is not guaranteed for calls inside classes or imported by alias (m08b, m08c survive).
